purpose: The CapabilityTask/PurposeTask ADAPTATION LADDER (doctrine: _repos/teleon/context/standards/capability-task-architecture-doctrine.md). Risk-tiered levels L0..L5 map a change type to the GATE it must pass and whether a HUMAN must approve. Encodes the CORE INVARIANT: a task may adapt its MEANS (L0-L3, auto if gates pass) but may NEVER autonomously change its ENDS (L5, always human-gated). Deny-by-default: an UNKNOWN change type is treated as L5 (human-gated), never auto. Single source — the classifier (_repos/baltor/backend/src/baltor/purpose_tasks/adaptation_ladder.py) + the proof read this; no parallel literal.
control_rule: Branch on the numeric LEVEL + the gate, never on a change-name string. Higher level ⇒ stricter gate; auto-promotion is only for L0-L3 (MEANS) and only when the gate passes; L4-L5 (decomposition / ENDS) always require a human.

levels.name: implementation_candidate
levels.note: new code/workflow/tool sequence; full eval + provenance + canary + rollback

levels.name: capability_decomposition
levels.note: structural change to the capability graph; human approval

levels.name: boundary_expansion
levels.note: redraws the box (the ENDS); ALWAYS human-approved

_forbidden_note: These can NEVER be an autonomous candidate adaptation (they weaken the contract / hide the truth). Changing them at all is a deliberate human CapabilityBoundaryChange to the contract itself (L5), never a candidate promotion. The classifier returns may_auto_promote=false for them.
_ends_note: The CORE INVARIANT set — every 'ends' change must be human-gated (L5) or forbidden; none may auto-promote.
